records.subagent_summary: My 8 rollouts scored 1/8 (exec 149.398). Four burned the 16384-token cap with no box; the four that terminated wrong all boxed 143. New evidence: the incumbent's contrapositive did get echoed (pooled appears up to 27 times, 'two distinct' in 6 rollouts) yet no rollout ever finished a pooled list. Instead the dominant path is a global case split - open sum-reading and product-reading, check each is consistent with both statements, find BOTH are, then declare a winner on looks (one explicitly called 14x143 'unique', another invoked primality 30 times). That whole-reading consistency test is the trap: it never discriminates, so the rollout must guess. So this revision names and bans it up front, notes each unsettled option yields only one partner per v (making the list cheap to finish), and adds a survivor-count audit whose zero branch diagnoses the illegal fixing rather than licensing a guess.

records.mutation: predict-the-locus-shape-from-a-conic-classification-table and make that match the only check; move the ratio-form ban upstream into the derivation
records.subagent_summary: 8/8 correct, so train is saturated (train_i 1.0) and the lever is transfer plus wasted budget. Every rollout had the modulus ratio and the completed-square circle inside its first ~2k chars, then spent 4-8x more tokens on verification the incumbent bans only at the end: all 8 rewrote to ratio form and nth-rooted it into per-solution branches (10-41 exponential expressions each). The worst (6590 tokens, 25 hedges, 12 'mistake', 6 'contradiction') mis-solved a branch, got a point failing its own modulus ratio, then doubted the modulus law itself for ~4k tokens. Three others closed by calling the condition 'necessary and sufficient': right answer, wrong logic that will not transfer. Diagnosis: a terminal ban leaves the checking urge nowhere legal. So the ratio ban moves upstream into the derivation, and the urge is redirected to a free portable check: classify the locus shape from the condition's form before any algebra, then require only that the completed square match it.

1/8 correct. No rollout ever computed a clipped area: shoelace appears 0 times in all 8. Three failures used the wedge frame yet ruled by prose: two said the cover "lies outside" S (overlap 0, answered summed areas) and one said S lies wholly inside the aligned cover (overlap = area(S)); each cited coordinate ranges that visibly straddle 0 without comparing them. Four hit the 16384 cap: they reached the right clipped value early, then re-litigated rotation (104-196 rotation mentions, 18-38 tangency) and never boxed. The lone winner reached the same value and closed. The incumbent asserts sign facts ("one negative coordinate kills containment") but never asks for numbers, so nothing is executed. This revision demands numeric vertices then an axis-by-axis range intersection, which refutes both the disjoint and the containment verdict from the same table, and orders shoelace-then-box before any angle talk.

8/8 correct with the incumbent, so aggregation is sound; the cost is one shared detour. All 8 rollouts built a difference operator on the board (P(n+1)-P(n) or P(x+1)-P(x)), demanded it be constant for ALL n, got a degree d-1 polynomial, and concluded "must be linear/constant" - 98 hits total, up to 37 in one rollout - then had to recover. Six also called the product "too large" (18 hits) and reopened tightness. Spend was 8.0k-15.3k tokens with 207 "Wait" restarts; earlier rounds show these loops truncate when they start sooner. The incumbent only bans chaining adjacent terms, justified by "neighbours may differ", which round 19 found is misparsed as "each term needs a distinct polynomial". This revision instead names the real logical error - promoting finitely many point conditions to an identity in x - voids the "must be linear" conclusion outright, and keeps the per-group cap, the sum, and the substitution certificate.

6/8 correct (149.402); both failures hit the 16384-token cap on the SAME stage, forming the closure equation, and never reached the incumbent's root test. One slipped arithmetic inside the shifted argument (wrote t-4/3+1 as t+1/3), so its quadratic had irrational roots and the given vertex was not a root; it never tested that, and spent the rest of the budget on diagonal-midpoint restatements (15 mentions). The other inverted the factor by treating log_{1/2}A+1 as log_{1/2}(2A), got discriminant -92, then declared the problem impossible (8 'no real' passages, 15 midpoint mentions). Its earlier attempt produced a polynomial whose ONLY roots were the two given vertices, another detectable-equation bug. So the revision moves validation upstream: check the closure numerically at a given vertex before any algebra, and route failure to the shift or the factor, not to the problem.

0/8. Part b is the graded quantity and all 8 missed it. Seven (idx 0-5,7) explicitly wrote that the shed's bottom bag is the one carried LAST, then answered 1/4 by symmetry: 'each bag equally likely to move last' or 3!/4! over random permutations. Idx 6 declared the order always reversed (1, 0). Part a was template-guessed: 1/2^(n-1) (idx 0,1,2,5), 1/24 (idx 4,7), 1/256 (idx 3). Not one rollout wrote a concrete move order with per-step legality, so the incumbent's forced/free pricing never gets executed. The incumbent states arrival-rank orientation declaratively and loses to the flip every round. This revision makes the position-to-arrival-time translation a required written line with an explicit self-catch test, and trims length back toward the 91-token variant that holds the best held-out so far, since every rewrite at 175-192 tokens scored held-out 0.2 or worse.

records.mutation: require-displayed-elimination-per-toy+first-thing-on-page-ordering-gate (asserted/recalled toy values are inadmissible; no general-size algebra until three exact solutions are shown)
records.subagent_summary: 0/8; 6 hit the 16384 cap. Root cause is new: not one rollout ever solved a small case. Six wrote zero small systems and went straight to full-size symbolic work (48-142 'coefficient of x' mentions, 51-80 of 2004!, Vandermonde/elementary-symmetric detours) and never emitted an answer. The two that terminated only *asserted* toy answers with no arithmetic shown -- one claimed n=3,4 give 1/2 and 1/3 and shipped 1/(n-1); the other claimed -1, 1/2, -1/4 and shipped a power-of-2 law. So the incumbent's ladder is skipped or faked, and its bans on stated-size algebra are ignored because nothing competes for the first line. This revision makes the smallest numeric case the mandatory first thing written, makes a toy value admissible only with its elimination displayed, gates law-fitting behind three displayed solutions, and keeps the proven consecutive-ratio law.

7/8 public rollouts scored 1 (train_i 0.875). The single failure never doubted the gcd machinery; it mis-assigned roles, reading each listed village-wide figure as a per-house cost. That made total = 525*N with total already 525, so N collapsed to 1, the integrality condition did no work, and it answered a bare cost*1.2. It burned most of 8242 tokens cycling per-house/per-street readings and calling each a contradiction. The incumbent's only defence is 'decide once whether each figure is a grand total or a per-unit amount', which tells the student to stop revisiting but not how to pick. Prior negative screens against bad readings (self-refutation, well-posedness, role-locking) all lost held-out ground, whereas the kept rounds added constructive machinery. So I swapped the passive clause for a constructive setup: name a per-unit unknown per figure and write figure = N x unknown, which fixes aggregates as aggregates by construction and makes integrality bind on the unknowns.

7/8 correct (3.5k-5.4k tokens). The one failure hit the 16384-token cap. It centered correctly, then mis-nested the composition (re-cubing an already-cubed offset: BA^9, so B^2=A^8, B=+-A^4, 16 mentions; 120 r^3 mentions). Both corrupted branches gave high-degree equations in the center, and it spent most of its budget trial-substituting integer centers (2,3,4,5,6,-2,-3,30), then fell back to generic coefficient matching and died in a degenerate repeated-subtraction loop. All 7 correct rollouts reached A^3=B^3 on their first page and closed in one line. Rounds 9/10 (exponent audits), 14/15 (factoring), 16 (no-ratio), 17 (validate-vs-p=q), 18 (conjugation) and 19 (elimination order) all added corrective wording about that same slip and all lost heldout. So this revision leaves the proven spine intact and adds a positive escape hatch instead: name the classification of commuting polynomial families, giving a concrete next move when the centered form does not fit.

records.subagent_summary: 6/8 wrong. idx1, idx6, idx7 never wrote a state: each sub-step became a transposition, the composite was called disjoint transpositions or an involution, and they boxed 2. idx7 also placed the blocks wrong, writing the length-2 block swap as (1 2)(3 4) - swapping inside a block, not block-to-block - manufacturing the disjointness. idx5 invented per-size cycle lists (6-cycle plus 2-cycle, then an 8-cycle), got 2,4,6,8, boxed 2n. idx4 fabricated 2,4,10,30 and fit a product of primes. idx2 had a correct small-size state trace, then built a permutation table giving order 2 and burned all 16k tokens arguing table versus states. Both correct rollouts just simulated whole repeats on lettered words. The incumbent invites the lcm-of-cycle-lengths cross-check that caused three failures, so the revision bans cycle notation, gives the exact j to j+L block rule with no intra-block swap, a two-repeat order-2 refutation, and a grow-and-divide filter.
